summary: Iteration 16 backend verification: NEW endpoint POST /api/readings/reset (server.py L452-483) fully verified. Added 11 tests under TestResetReadings covering: 401 without JWT and 401 with invalid JWT; 400 with Arabic detail 'نطاق غير صالح ...' for scope=invalid and scope=<empty>; default scope='month' when no query param; scope='month' deletes only current UTC-calendar-month readings and preserves previous-month readings; scope='month' brings GET /api/stats/dashboard.total_monthly_kwh down to 0 for a freshly-seeded customer; scope='all' deletes every reading (GET /api/readings returns [] and Mongo readings collection empty); scope='month' does NOT touch customers or invoices; readings still writable after 'all' reset (regression); dashboard shape intact after resets. Response shape verified: {message, deleted_count:int, scope:'month'|'all'}. Full suite: 105/105 PASSED (100%) in ~25s. No regressions across auth, customers, generators, readings, invoices, payments, expenses, dashboard.

minor.issue: Uses datetime.utcnow() with naive datetimes and calendar-month bucketing. If MongoDB reading_date is stored in a different TZ (e.g., server local), month-boundary edge cases could over/under-delete near midnight UTC. Current codebase stores UTC everywhere so it's fine, but a tz-aware helper would be safer.
Destructive endpoint accepts no confirmation token/csrf; JWT is the only guard. Consider requiring an explicit body flag like {"confirm": true} to prevent accidental client-side triggers.

scope is a raw string. Prefer Literal['month','all'] or Enum so FastAPI returns 422 automatically and OpenAPI documents the allowed values. Current implementation returns a nice Arabic 400 instead — acceptable but less discoverable.

Deleting readings does NOT recalculate customer.current_balance or invalidate invoices computed from those readings. Depending on product intent, resetting the kWh counter while leaving invoices intact could confuse users. Flag for product review, not a bug per spec.
(carried) status query param not whitelisted; is_overdue update loop is O(N) update_one — prefer update_many.
(carried) No amount>0 validation; expense_type still free-form (no Enum).

OPTIONAL: Decide product-side whether resetting readings should also recompute customer balances / mark related invoices, or whether that separation is intentional.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py L452-483 POST /api/readings/reset: correctly (a) computes UTC current-month [start_date, end_date) window; (b) for scope='month' deletes readings whose reading_date is within that window and returns {message, deleted_count, scope:'month'}; (c) for scope='all' deletes everything and returns {message, deleted_count, scope:'all'}; (d) for anything else raises 400 with detail 'نطاق غير صالح. استخدم month أو all'. JWT required via api_router dependency.
Route ordering: POST /api/readings/reset is defined BEFORE GET /api/readings/{reading_id}, so no ObjectId parsing shadows the string 'reset' — verified via tests (no unexpected 400/404).
Only touches db.readings collection — non-destructive w.r.t. customers, invoices, payments, expenses (regression-tested).
seed_data_creation: None. All tests create TEST_RESET_* customers and clean them up inline via DELETE /api/customers/{id} (which cascades readings/invoices/payments).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 16 added POST /api/readings/reset?scope=month|all (server.py L452-483). It only mutates db.readings. TestResetReadings (11 tests) covers auth, invalid-scope 400, default scope, month-window correctness (current vs previous month), dashboard total_monthly_kwh reduction, scope='all' empties collection, and cross-collection non-interference. Full suite: 105 tests, ~25s, all green. NOTE: TestResetReadings runs LAST in file order, and its scope='all' tests WILL wipe every reading created by earlier customers — but since prior test classes cascade-delete their own customers (and thus readings) as they go, this is safe. If a future test class is inserted AFTER TestResetReadings that depends on readings being present, move it before, or add setup that reseeds readings.
